extracted.intended_audience: general readers interested in fact-checking and political/media accountability (PolitiFact audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A chronological, sourced timeline that tracks a public figure's repeated statements about a specific event, showing how the account evolved and linking to primary transcripts, broadcasts, blog posts and news reports. Used to support fact-checking and assign a veracity rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth-O-Meter rating categories
rubrics_metrics.description: PolitiFact's Truth-O-Meter labels shown on the page: "True, Mostly True, Half True, Mostly False, False, Pants on Fire, Full Flop, Half Flip, No Flip."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the site's categorical verdicts used to classify the veracity of statements and to filter/browse related items. The page exposes these labels as the standard rating taxonomy for evaluating claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Our Sources (citation of reporting and primary materials)
rubrics_metrics.description: A clearly listed set of sources used to support the timeline and reporting (examples on this page include Stars and Stripes; Washington Post; Slate; BuzzFeed; Fox; CNN; NBC; WNYC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The timeline attaches or cites primary source material (transcripts, broadcast segments, blog posts, news stories, and interviews) to substantiate each dated entry. The presence of an explicit 'Our Sources' section signals the expectation that factual timelines cite verifiable reporting and primary documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chronological presentation of statements with contextual excerpts
rubrics_metrics.description: The page presents entries by date (e.g., March 26, 2003; Sept. 27, 2007; March 26, 2013; Jan. 30, 2015; Feb. 4, 2015), and for each entry includes quoted excerpts or paraphrases of what was said and the medium (transcript, book, blog, interview, broadcast).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good timeline practice shown here: provide precise dates, identify the medium/source for each version of the statement, include direct quotes or close paraphrases, and note changes/uncertainties in the account over time to show evolution of the claim.
